title: Police cleared in fatal shooting after chase
article: The Special Investigations Unit says there are no reasonable grounds to lay charges against two provincial police officers in the fatal shooting of an eastern Ontario man in July 2009.
The SIU says the incident began on the evening of July 3, when 35-year-old Jeffrey Charbonneau fled a RIDE program stop on Highway 401 in Brockville, Ont.
Officers at the RIDE program began a pursuit that reached speeds of 150 km/h on a county road, the SIU said Wednesday.
During the pursuit, the Hammond, Ont., man ran a red light, drove around two civilian vehicles on the shoulder, and forced an oncoming car off the road.
Charbonneau continued to drive even after a spike belt punctured the front tires of his truck.
A total of six police vehicles surrounded Charbonneau after a rolling block finally brought him to a stop more than 13 kilometres north of Highway 401.
In an apparent attempt to escape, Charbonneau began to ram the police vehicles directly behind and in front of him.
When Charbonneau eventually succeeded in creating enough space that he get his truck through, two subject officers discharged their firearms a total of eight times.
One of the bullets went through the driver's side mirror and struck Charbonneau in the head, killing him instantly, the SIU said.

"Due to the nature of bullet projectiles from the two identical police issue handguns, it is impossible to determine which of the two subject officers discharged which bullets and therefore which officer was responsible for causing the death of Mr. Charbonneau," said SIU director Ian Scott.
The officers also had "reasonable grounds" to believe Charbonneau would use any means necessary to continue fleeing, Scott said.
"Whichever subject officer fired the lethal shot was standing at such an angle to the pickup truck that it was almost directly in front of him and reasonably capable of running him over," he said.
The SIU is a civilian agency that investigates cases of serious injuries and deaths involving the police.
